formation.title: Regnum Illyricum
formation.text:
Split is ours. The palace of Diocletian, which has been a town inside a ruin for a thousand years, no longer flies the lion of Saint Mark, and the road up through the Klis pass is open to the interior. Far to the north the ban's officers sit at Zagreb, where Gradec on its hill and the bishop's Kaptol across the ravine have quarrelled for two centuries and are now told to be one city.

What is proclaimed here is not merely Croatia enlarged. The men who drafted the style are the same sort who read Pribojević of Hvar and Šišgorić of Šibenik: canons, notaries and city patricians who call their own speech Illyrian and themselves Illyrici, and who hold that this coast and this hinterland are the inheritors of the classical Illyricum. Rome has already granted them the name. In the church of San Girolamo degli Illirici the Mass is said by Slavonic-speaking priests, and the letters they read were given to Saint Jerome by legend and to the bishop of Senj by Innocent IV in fact.

The kingdom that stands up today has a wall on one side and a pulpit on the other, and it cannot afford both at full strength. Shall Illyria be the confines of the kingdom made permanent, garrisoned to the last valley and hard to everything beyond it? Or shall it be Rome's Slavonic province, spending on colleges and presses and sending its priests across the border rather than its cavalry?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the wall. Let it be built and manned.

modifiers.name: Confinia Regni
modifiers.text: The confines of the kingdom, in the Latin the Croatian chancery used for its own frontier districts. Garrisons are doubled, the approaches are stripped bare, and every valley that leads inland is watched by men who hold their fields on the condition that they watch it. A wall, however, makes no friends of the people standing on the wrong side of it, and a great many of them live within this realm.

options.text: Send the priest where the soldier cannot go.

modifiers.name: Sacrum Illyricum
modifiers.text: The Roman institutions of the Illyrian nation become the policy of the state. Colleges are endowed, presses are licensed, and priests are trained in a tongue their congregations already speak and sent where no bishop can follow them. Every ducat spent on a seminary is a ducat not spent on a regiment, and the muster rolls show it.

advances.name: The Glagoljaši
advances.text: In 1248 Innocent IV permitted the bishop of Senj and his clergy to celebrate the liturgy in Slavonic using Glagolitic letters, on the strength of a belief that Saint Jerome had invented the alphabet. The belief was wrong and the privilege was real. It created a class of married, half-lettered village priests, far more numerous than the Latin canons and far closer to the people they served.

event.title: The Tongue of Saint Jerome
event.text:
The privilege is old, oddly specific and entirely genuine. In 1248 Pope Innocent IV wrote to Filip, bishop of Senj, permitting the clergy of his diocese to celebrate the liturgy in the Slavonic tongue using the letters they called Glagolitic. The justification offered was that the alphabet had been devised by Saint Jerome, who was born in Dalmatia and was therefore one of ours. This is false. Jerome had nothing to do with it and the letters came from Moravia. It has also been believed for four hundred years, it is written into papal documents, and it is why the Illyrian church in Rome is dedicated to Saint Jerome and not to anybody else.

What it means on the ground is that a peasant in the Kvarner hills hears the Mass in words he understands, from a married village priest who owns perhaps three books and can read all of them. The cathedral canons, trained in Latin and jealous of their Latin, have never entirely made peace with this.

The chancery asks which clergy the crown intends to build on.

options.text: The glagoljaši. They are ours and they are heard.

modifiers.name: The Slavonic Rite
modifiers.text: The village priest keeps his missal in the angular letters, and the crown keeps the village priest. There are more of them than there are canons, and they are believed.

options.text: Set learned Latin canons over every parish.

modifiers.name: The Latin Chapter
modifiers.text: A learned Latin chapter is placed over every Slavonic parish. Rome is pleased, the cathedral schools fill, and the country priest is told what his own missal means.

advances.name: The Vinodol Code
advances.text: Written down on the sixth of January 1288 by forty-two elected men of nine communities of the Vinodol valley, in Glagolitic and in their own speech, to settle exactly what the counts of Krk could and could not demand of them. It is not a town charter but a law of the countryside, and it is old enough that Russkaya Pravda is the only Slavic code that precedes it.

advances.name: The Banderia
advances.text: Before the kingdom had a standing frontier army it had the banners of its great houses: Šubić, Nelipić, Kurjaković, Frankopan, each turning out its own mailed retinue under its own arms. Magnificent, expensive, and answerable to a lord before a king.

advances.name: Banal Authority
advances.text: The ban was a viceroy in fact if not in title. He convoked the Sabor, led the banderium of the kingdom, minted in his own name in earlier centuries and judged in the king's. Croatia was a country that had to be governed with its own consent, and the office of ban was the machinery for obtaining it.

advances.name: The Sava Oakwoods
advances.text: The flood forests of the Sava and the Drava grow an oak slow, straight and close-grained enough that shipwrights and coopers will pay to have it carried a very long way. The grain of the Pannonian plain floats down the same rivers.

advances.name: The Thirtieth
advances.text: The tricesima, a royal customs of one part in thirty, taken at designated stations on the roads between the interior and the sea. It is the fiscal spine of a kingdom whose real product is the distance between the Sava and the Adriatic.

advances.name: The Peace of Zadar
advances.text: By the treaty sworn in the Franciscan sacristy at Zadar in February 1358, Venice renounced the entire Dalmatian coast and the doge struck duke of Dalmatia from his style. The cities came back to the crown, and every later Illyria inherits both the coast and the memory of losing it.

event.title: The Peace of Zadar
event.text:
It was settled in the sacristy of the Franciscan friary at Zadar on the eighteenth of February, 1358. Venice renounced the whole coast from the Kvarner to Dubrovnik, and the doge undertook to strike the words duke of Dalmatia and Croatia from his own title. No siege train achieved this. It was achieved by patient war, by Hungarian and Croatian arms in Italy, and by the plain fact that the cities themselves preferred a distant king to a near republic.

The communes now come back into the kingdom with their statutes in their hands: Split's of 1312, Zadar's of 1305, Šibenik's of 1379, each of them a book of self-government with an elected knez, a council and a settled contempt for outside judges.

The question in every council chamber from Trogir to Rab is what the crown means to do about those books.

options.text: Confirm every statute. Rule a coast that consents.

modifiers.name: The Communal Charters
modifiers.text: The coastal towns come back to the crown with their statutes confirmed, their councils intact and their customs their own. They pay, and they remember who let them keep their books.

options.text: One kingdom, one law. The ban judges in the cities.

modifiers.name: The Ban's Writ
modifiers.text: The ban's officers sit in the town halls of the coast, and the elected knez answers to them. The communes lose their old freedom of manoeuvre and the kingdom gains a shoreline it actually governs.

advances.name: The Glagolitic Notaries
advances.text: The privilege of 1248 was liturgical. Within a century it had become a habit of the whole public life of the littoral: leases, wills, boundary settlements and court records drawn in Glagolitic and in the vernacular, so that a man who could not read Latin could still have his own contract read back to him.

advances.name: The Pauline Hermits
advances.text: The one religious order founded within the Croatian and Hungarian kingdom, and the only one that could plausibly be called native. Their house at Lepoglava, endowed by the counts of Celje, kept the oldest grammar school in the country and eventually the best library in it.

advances.name: The Golden Bull of Gradec
advances.text: Béla IV, fleeing the Mongols, granted Gradec the status of a free royal town in 1242. It faced the bishop's fortified Kaptol across a ravine, feuded with it for the next three hundred years, occasionally burned it, and between the two of them they became Zagreb.

effects.name: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

advances.name: The Press at Senj
advances.text: The Glagolitic missal of 1483 was in print twenty-eight years after Gutenberg. Blaž Baromić learned the trade in Venice and brought it home, and the chapter press at Senj ran from 1494 to 1508. Nowhere else in Latin Europe was the Mass itself being set in type in a vernacular.

event.title: Eight Books in Fourteen Years
event.text:
The first Croatian Glagolitic missal came off a press on the twenty-second of February, 1483, twenty-eight years after Gutenberg finished his Bible, and nobody now knows for certain who printed it or where. What is certain is what happened next. In 1492 the chapter of Senj sent the priest Blaž Baromić to Venice to learn the trade; he worked in Torresani's shop, helped print a Glagolitic breviary in 1493, and came home with the knowledge. The press at Senj ran from 1494 until 1508 and produced eight books. A generation later Šimun Kožičić Benja, bishop of Modruš, set up a second press in his own house at Rijeka and printed six more in the space of thirteen months.

Eight books, then six. It is a small output by the standards of Venice, which was printing that many in a fortnight. It is also the only place in Latin Christendom where the Mass itself was being set in type in a vernacular and in an alphabet no Roman could read.

The canons ask for a further grant of paper and lead.

options.text: Let the press run. The letters are our title deed.

modifiers.name: The Press at Senj
modifiers.text: A chapter of canons on a windy Adriatic rock owns a printing press and uses it to print the Mass in Slavonic. Nowhere else in Latin Christendom is that legal.

advances.name: Bosna Srebrena
advances.text: The Franciscan custody of Bosnia, founded in 1340, was the only institution of the Latin church to survive the conquest of 1463. Fra Anđeo Zvizdović obtained a charter of protection from Mehmed II at Milodraž, and for four centuries the friars were the only church Catholic Bosnia had.

event.title: The Charter of Milodraž
event.text:
The kingdom of Bosnia ended in 1463 in the space of a summer. King Stjepan Tomašević was taken at Ključ and beheaded, the great fortresses opened one after another, and Mehmed rode through a country that had had its own crown a year before.

What survived, alone, was the Franciscan custody of Bosna Srebrena, founded in 1340 to work among the Bosnian Church and now the only institution of the Latin church left standing in the province. Its guardian, Fra Anđeo Zvizdović, went to the sultan's camp at Milodraž and came away with a charter: the friars were not to be molested, their houses were not to be taken, and those who followed them were to keep their property and their worship. The document has been kept at Fojnica ever since and produced, again and again, in front of Ottoman judges who did not expect it to exist.

For four centuries the friars will be the only bishops Bosnia has. The chancery must decide whether that is a foundation or an insult.

options.text: The friars hold Bosnia. Fund them and be patient.

modifiers.name: The Friars' Charter
modifiers.text: The brown habits go where the crown cannot. Under the sultan's own charter the Franciscans keep the Catholics of Bosnia in the faith, and the crown keeps a channel into a province it does not hold.

options.text: Bosnia is a stolen crown. Prepare to take it back.

modifiers.name: The Bosnian Claim
modifiers.text: Bosnia is entered in the chancery as a stolen kingdom rather than a mission field. The gunners measure the walls of Jajce, the border captains are told what a Christian province is worth, and the friars are told to wait.

effects.name: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency
Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle

advances.name: Antemurale Christianitatis
advances.text: Leo X gave the kingdom the title in a letter to ban Petar Berislavić in 1519. It was flattery with an obligation attached. Krbava Field in 1493 had already shown what the wall cost when it failed, and it would go on failing at intervals for the next two centuries.

advances.name: The Chapter Walls
advances.text: Between 1512 and 1520 the canons of Zagreb walled their own cathedral precinct with towers and a ditch while the town below remained open. The pattern repeated across the kingdom until the chapter house was routinely the last defensible building in the parish.

advances.name: Judita
advances.text: Marko Marulić of Split finished it on the twenty-second of April 1501 and had it printed at Venice in 1521: the story of Judith and Holofernes in Croatian verse, aimed squarely at a people under Ottoman attack. He wrote in Latin for Europe, was read by Thomas More and Francis Xavier, and wrote in the vernacular for home.

advances.name: De Origine Slavorum
advances.text: Vinko Pribojević stood up before the nobles of Hvar in 1525 and told them they were Illyrians, that Alexander's Macedonians had been their kin, and that every Slav from the Adriatic to the Volga was of one blood with them. Printed at Venice in 1532, expanded by Mavro Orbini of Ragusa in 1601, the claim gave a scattered Catholic people a single name to answer to.

advances.name: The Haramije
advances.text: Raised in 1539 as paid foot for the Croatian and Slavonian forts, with one specific task: to run down the Ottoman martolos raiders who crossed the border to take people and sell them. It was a war of abduction, and the haramije were the answer to it.

advances.name: The Military Frontier
advances.text: Organised from 1553 into the Croatian and Slavonian generalcies, the Krajina held land in hereditary tenure against hereditary service. Whole populations were moved into it to garrison it, and in time the cordon became a society with its own law, its own captains and no landlords at all.

event.title: Who Pays for the Cordon
event.text:
The frontier has stopped being an event and become a place. From the Adriatic at Senj to the Drava it is now a permanent belt of forts, watch-houses within sight of one another and settled soldier villages, organised from 1553 into the generalcies of Croatia and Slavonia. The men in it hold their land free of dues in return for hereditary service, turn out at the alarm gun, and are a standing army in everything but name.

It is also ruinously expensive, and the Sabor cannot pay for it. The estates of Styria, Carinthia and Carniola can, and have offered. They will not, however, pay for soldiers commanded from Zagreb.

This is the constitutional question of the age, dressed as an accounting problem. Whoever pays the Krajina owns it, and whoever owns it owns the border.

options.text: Take the Austrian money. Walls first, pride after.

modifiers.name: The Graz Subsidy
modifiers.text: The inner Austrian estates pay for the cordon, so the cordon obeys the inner Austrian estates. The soldiers are cheap, well supplied and no longer entirely the crown's.

options.text: The frontier is the kingdom's. We will find the money.

modifiers.name: The Banal Frontier
modifiers.text: The frontier stays under the ban and the Sabor, and so does the bill. A kingdom that pays for its own walls may also decide where they run.

advances.name: Karlstadt
advances.text: Laid out in 1579 on empty meadow at the meeting of the Kupa and the Korana, a six-pointed star with a grid inside it and a garrison paid by the estates of Inner Austria. The frontier's one purpose-built fortress town, and still recognisably its own plan.

advances.name: The Illyrian Colleges
advances.text: Gregory XIII opened the Illyrian College at Loreto in 1580; Sixtus V rebuilt San Girolamo degli Illirici in Rome and confirmed its chapter of Slavonic-speaking priests by the bull Sapientiam Sanctorum in 1589. Both existed to make clergy who could go home to lands where no bishop could travel.

event.title: Colleges for a Nation Under Another Crown
event.text:
In 1580 Gregory XIII founded the Illyrian College at Loreto and gave it to the Jesuits, so that boys from the Slavic lands could be made into priests capable of going home again. In 1589 Sixtus V, who had already rebuilt the church of San Girolamo degli Illirici in Rome, confirmed by the bull Sapientiam Sanctorum a chapter of Slavonic-speaking priests attached to it. Bologna, Fermo and Ancona followed with foundations of their own.

The purpose was never in doubt. Marin Temperica had written to the Jesuit general in 1582 that a single Slavic tongue would carry a preacher from the Adriatic to the Black Sea, and that the order should print the grammars and dictionaries to fix it. The colleges existed to make missionaries for the lands under Ottoman rule, and by any honest accounting they underperformed. They also produced parish priests, bishops and writers for three centuries.

Our own foundation now takes its first intake, and someone must decide where its graduates are sent.

options.text: Across the border. That is what they were made for.

modifiers.name: The Mission Beyond the Border
modifiers.text: Graduates of Loreto and San Girolamo cross into the sultan's lands with a breviary, a false name and a route home. They send back more than souls.

options.text: To our own parishes. Charity begins at the altar.

modifiers.name: A Clergy of Our Own
modifiers.text: The colleges keep their graduates for home altars. The kingdom gains the best educated parish clergy on this side of the Adriatic and the Congregation in Rome gains nothing.

advances.name: The Illyrian Grammar
advances.text: Faust Vrančić of Šibenik printed his dictionary of five noble European tongues at Venice in 1595. Bartol Kašić of Pag published Institutionum linguae Illyricae at Rome in 1604 on the order of the Jesuit general, because a missionary needed one Illyrian that a Bosnian and a Dalmatian would both accept.

advances.name: The Scala of Split
advances.text: Daniel Rodriga spent a decade persuading Venice, and in 1592 the scala at Split opened with its customhouse and its quarantine. The Bosnian pasha agreed to let the caravans turn that way, and the overland trade of the Balkans acquired an Adriatic terminus.

advances.name: The Croats
advances.text: Some twenty thousand Croat light horse rode in Imperial service at the height of the German war, most of Wallenstein's harquebusiers among them. They scouted, pursued, cut convoys and burned country, and the French borrowed the scarf they knotted at the throat and named it after them.

event.title: The Knot at the Throat
event.text:
The Germans call them Crabaten and cannot decide whether they are cavalry or a plague. At the height of the war in the Empire something like twenty thousand of them are riding under Imperial colours, most of Wallenstein's harquebusiers among them, and their work is scouting, pursuit, the cutting of convoys and the burning of anything that might feed an enemy the following week. Set them against a line of pike and shot and they will not stand; ask them to ruin a province and it will be ruined.

The French, who have fought them and hired them, noticed the linen scarf knotted at the throat of the officers, took it up, and named it after the men who wore it. The regiments will outlast the war, the war will outlast the century, and the scarf will outlast both.

The muster is confirmed and the standards are issued.

options.text: Let them ride. The Empire will pay to be frightened.

modifiers.name: The Croat Regiments
modifiers.text: Light horse who scout further, ride harder and burn more thoroughly than anything the Empire can raise for itself. Paris has already stolen the scarf they wear at the throat.

advances.name: The Magnates' Conspiracy
advances.text: Petar Zrinski and Fran Krsto Frankopan, convinced that Vienna had sold the frontier at Vasvár, conspired with France, Venice, Poland and finally the Porte, and were betrayed by all of them. They were beheaded at Wiener Neustadt on the thirtieth of April 1671 and the greatest estates in Croatia passed to the chamber.

event.title: Wiener Neustadt
event.text:
Petar Zrinski was ban of Croatia and his brother-in-law Fran Krsto Frankopan was the last of a house that had held Krk and the Kvarner since anyone could remember. Between them they controlled a third of the kingdom. Convinced that Vienna had sold the frontier to the sultan at Vasvár and would go on selling it, they spent seven years in correspondence with the French, the Venetians, the Poles and finally the Turks themselves, and they were betrayed by every one of them in turn.

They came to Vienna under safe conduct in 1670 to beg pardon. On the thirtieth of April 1671 both were beheaded in the courtyard at Wiener Neustadt, and their estates, which were the estates of half of Croatia, passed to the chamber.

The sentence is signed. What is not yet settled is whether the crown carries it out.

options.text: Let the sentence stand. Take the lands with the heads.

modifiers.name: The Confiscation
modifiers.text: Two heads, and the lands of two houses that had been great since before the kingdom had a ban. The crown is suddenly the largest landowner in Croatia, and the nobility will not forget how it happened.

options.text: Pardon them. A magnate who owes you his neck is loyal.

modifiers.name: The Reconciled Magnates
modifiers.text: The sentences are read out and then commuted. The great houses keep their lands and their heads, and thereafter serve a crown that could have taken both.

advances.name: The Recovery of Slavonia
advances.text: Karlowitz in 1699 returned Slavonia and Syrmia to the crown, emptied by a century and a half of raiding and grown back to oak forest. What followed was not conquest but settlement: colonists brought in by the wagonload, and frontier regiments planted on the new line.

advances.name: The Free Port
advances.text: Rijeka and Bakar were declared free ports in 1719. For the first time the Pannonian interior had a saltwater outlet that it owned outright rather than rented from a republic across the water.

advances.name: The Carolina Road
advances.text: Driven from Karlovac over the Gorski Kotar to Bakar between 1726 and 1732 by the engineer Anton Matthias Weiss, it was the first road across those mountains a loaded wagon could take. Everything before it went over the passes on a packhorse.

advances.name: The Parish Schools
advances.text: The village priest taught the village children their letters, and the letters he taught were the ones in his own missal. Literacy in this kingdom spread outward from the altar rather than downward from the court, and it reached people no court school would have admitted.

advances.name: The Josephina and the Louisiana
advances.text: The Josephina reached Senj in 1779 and the Lujzijana reached Rijeka in 1811, each straighter and better graded than the last, until a cart could cross from the Sava to the Adriatic in a few days. The wealth of this kingdom was always the distance between them.

advances.name: The Seminary at Zadar
advances.text: Matej Karaman, archbishop of Zadar, printed a corrected Glagolitic missal at Rome in 1741 and founded a seminary in 1748 to train priests who could actually read it. The privilege of 1248 was five hundred years old and still being taught to boys.

advances.name: The Rjecoslozje
advances.text: Joakim Stulli of Ragusa spent fifty years on his lexicon and had it printed between 1801 and 1810: some eighty thousand words of Illyrian set against Latin and Italian, the last and largest monument of the learned Illyrian idea before politics took the word away from the scholars.

advances.name: The Urbarial Settlement
advances.text: The peasants of Severin rose in 1755 and the answer was an urbarium: a written schedule of what a tenant owed his lord and, more remarkably, of what he did not. The obligations of the Croatian and Slavonian countryside were fixed on paper and could thereafter be argued about in court.

advances.name: The Royal Academy
advances.text: The Jesuits were suppressed in 1773 and their Zagreb college became the Royal Academy of Sciences in 1776, a crown institution assembled out of a dissolved order's library, lecture rooms and unemployed professors.

destiny.name: The Crown of the Illyrian Nation
destiny.text: Illyria is proclaimed, and the argument that produced it is now a policy. One treasury cannot garrison every valley and endow every college at the same time, and the course taken at the proclamation is the course the chancery will keep entering in the register until it is finished. Required: stability 25.

event.title: What the Kingdom Is For
event.text:
The chancery has a habit it learned from the notaries: whatever has been decided is written down at once, so that nobody may later claim it was decided otherwise. The clerks enter the crown's course in the register, Latin on the left and the angular letters on the right, and the entry will be read aloud at every Sabor for as long as there is a Sabor to read it to.

Beyond the last watch-house the country is the same country. The same karst, the same oak, the same villages where the priest is married and the Mass is understood. The line drawn through it is a decision rather than a geography, and a decision can be moved.

What follows is the working out of a choice already made.

options.text: Enter it in the register.

destiny.name: Beyond the Drava
destiny.text: The Drava is not a frontier. It is a road, and the sanjak on the far bank exists to use it: a raiding country with its seat at Pécs and its crossing at Mohács, which has been harvesting Slavonia every summer since 1543. A wall defended from behind it is a wall that is climbed over. Required: own Pécs and Mohács, an army of 30,000 men.

conditions.text: Chose the Confines of the Kingdom destiny
Own Pécs, or a subject owns it
Own Mohács, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Sanjak Across the River
event.text:
For a century and a half the summer began the same way. The water dropped, the fords opened, and the horsemen of the sanjak whose seat is Pécs came over the Drava into Slavonia, took what could be driven and whoever could be sold, and were back across before the ban's banderium had finished assembling.

This year the crossing is made in the other direction. Mohács, where a king and an army were lost in an afternoon in 1526, is entered without a battle; the vineyards on the Villány hills are counted and taxed; and the garrisons that were the raiders' winter quarters become the northernmost posts of the kingdom's own line.

The frontier has moved for the first time in living memory, and it moved forward.

options.text: Garrison the fords. Let them learn the new arithmetic.

destiny.name: Alba Graeca
destiny.text: The chancery calls the white fortress at the confluence Alba Graeca and the rest of Christendom calls it the key. Whoever holds the meeting of the Sava and the Danube decides where the next war will be fought, and the crossing at Šabac decides who reaches the meeting. Required: own Šabac and Belgrade, an army of 50,000 men, Belgrade built up to 38 development.

conditions.text: Own Šabac, or a subject owns it
Own Belgrad, or a subject owns it
Belgrade is ours and its development is at least 38

event.title: Alba Graeca
event.text:
The confluence has been taken. Where the Sava runs into the Danube there is a limestone ridge with a fortress on it that Hungarians called Nándorfehérvár, that the chancery enters as Alba Graeca, and that every diplomat in Europe simply calls the key, because the road to Vienna begins at it and so does the road to Constantinople. Šabac, the crossing that made the approach possible, is being rebuilt with a proper ravelin.

With the line this long a question that could be postponed while it was short can be postponed no longer. The men who hold it are Vlach and Orthodox, refugees settled generations ago on empty ground, who take no landlord, obey their own headmen, and are the best light troops in the Christian world. They have petitioned, again, to have their liberties put in writing.

options.text: Grant the statutes. Let the frontier govern itself.

modifiers.name: Statuta Valachorum
modifiers.text: The frontier households receive their privileges in writing: their own headmen, their own courts, their land free of any landlord, and in return a musket in every house and a man at every muster. The crown gains an army it does not have to pay and a province that never quite finishes joining the kingdom.

options.text: No charter. The line is a command, not a privilege.

modifiers.name: The Generalcy
modifiers.text: No charter, no privileges, no headmen. The cordon is a command with commissioned officers, inspected magazines and rolls that are actually called. What it lacks in enthusiasm it makes up by being where it was ordered to be.

destiny.name: The Banat Cordon
destiny.text: The line now runs unbroken from the Adriatic to the mountains of Transylvania: watch-houses within sight of one another, crossings that are licensed or closed, and a population that holds its fields on the condition that it turns out at the alarm gun. A kingdom that pays for this out of its own treasury does not take its orders from anybody else's. Unlocks the Frontier Council. Required: own Timișoara and Smederevo, an army of 75,000 men, prestige 75, and 8 border locations fortified with Frontier Blockhouses or a fort.

conditions.text: Own Timișoara, or a subject owns it
Own Smederevo, or a subject owns it
At least 8 of our border locations are fortified with Frontier Blockhouses or a fort

event.title: The Line Complete
event.text:
It is finished. From the Adriatic to the Transylvanian passes there is now a continuous belt of watch-houses, blockhouses, licensed crossings and soldier villages, each within sight of the next, manned by families who hold their land for exactly one reason. Timișoara and its drained marshes are in the belt. So is Smederevo on the Danube. A courier can ride the whole length of it without once leaving the crown's jurisdiction.

What nobody in Graz expected is that the bill was paid here. The archduke's subsidy was declined, the estates voted the money, and the line belongs to the kingdom that holds it.

The war council, which now sits in our own capital, asks what the line is for.

options.text: Seal it. Nothing crosses but where we say it crosses.

modifiers.name: The Cordon Sealed
modifiers.text: The line is closed. Goods cross at licensed stations under guard and nowhere else, the fortresses are built to a plan rather than to a panic, and the merchants who used to slip over the hills at night now pay for the privilege of not doing so. Our own factors abroad cost rather more to keep.

options.text: March it. The best foot in Europe should not sit still.

modifiers.name: The Frontier Marches
modifiers.text: The cordon's regiments are lent to other people's wars and come home knowing things. Light foot who skirmish in broken country, live off it, and re-form after a beating faster than any line regiment in Europe.

destiny.name: The Congregation of Propaganda
destiny.text: Rome founds the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith in 1622, and four years later its polyglot press begins cutting type in every alphabet the missions need, the angular letters of Senj among them. The kingdom makes itself that congregation's workshop: presses, paper, seminaries and the men to staff them, paid for at home because nobody else will pay for them. Required: paper made in 2 of your locations, books produced or traded in one of your markets, gold 1000.

conditions.text: Paper is made in at least 2 of our locations, by a paper guild, workshop, manufactory or mill
A market the country is in

children.text: Books is produced in the market
Books is traded in the market

event.title: The Polyglot Press
event.text:
In a room off the Piazza di Spagna the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith keeps a press with more alphabets than any printing house on earth: Greek, Syriac, Armenian, Arabic, Coptic, Cyrillic, and the angular Glagolitic that has been legal in this kingdom and nowhere else since 1248. The punches for it were cut to a Dalmatian hand.

The arrangement that follows is not charity in either direction. Rome supplies the licence, the standard and the prestige. This kingdom supplies the paper, the endowments, the seminaries and, above all, the men: priests who can preach in a Slavic tongue and pass for locals from the Sava to the Danube, which is precisely what the Congregation cannot recruit anywhere else in Latin Christendom.

The treasury notes, without enthusiasm, what it costs.

options.text: Set the type. We will supply the men and the paper.

destiny.name: The Union of Marča
destiny.text: Simeon Vratanja went to Rome in 1611 and came home a bishop in Roman obedience with his own liturgy untouched. The monastery of Marča becomes the seat of a union eparchy for the Orthodox herdsmen who garrison the frontier, and the most dangerous population in the kingdom becomes, on paper, Catholic. Required: gold 2000, an Illyrian College or a library standing, and an average literacy of 20.

conditions.text: An Illyrian College or a library stands in one of our locations

event.title: The Bishop at Marča
event.text:
The monastery stands in the Slavonian frontier country, and the man who has just come back to it from Rome is a bishop twice over. Simeon Vratanja went as the spiritual head of the Orthodox Vlachs who garrison the border; he returned confirmed by the pope, in obedience to Rome, and with his own liturgy, his own calendar and his own married clergy untouched.

Every interested party regards this as a victory and no two of them agree on what has been won. Rome has a union. The Vlachs have a bishop of their own and a written guarantee of their rite. The chapter at Zagreb has a rival prelate inside its diocese and has already begun writing letters about it, and will still be writing them a century from now.

The crown must decide which reading is the official one.

options.text: A settlement. Confirm him, and confirm the rite.

modifiers.name: The Bishop at Marča
modifiers.text: The herdsmen keep their liturgy, their calendar and their own prelate, and enter Roman obedience on those terms. Their flocks feed the frontier and their sons fill its companies. The chapter at Zagreb regards the arrangement as an outrage and says so in writing, at length, for a hundred years.

options.text: A stage. Latin bishops, and Roman schools.

modifiers.name: The Latin Obedience
modifiers.text: The union is read as a waystation rather than a settlement. Latin bishops are set over the frontier parishes, the schools teach the Roman rite, and conversion proceeds steadily. The muster takes noticeably longer to assemble than it used to, and nobody will say why.

destiny.name: The Illyrian Church
destiny.text: Riceputi and Farlati begin the Illyricum Sacrum, a register of every see in Illyricum from the apostles onward, at the moment the crown reaches the province the geographers still call by that name. Shkodër and Lezha come under a Catholic king, and so does the mission archbishopric at Skopje, so that priests trained at Loreto no longer serve at the sultan's pleasure. Unlocks the Marian Shrine. Required: own the whole Illyria province, own Skopje, gold 3000, prestige 75.

conditions.text: Own Skopje, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Register of the Illyrian Church
event.text:
Two Jesuits in Venice are compiling, see by see and bishop by bishop, the entire ecclesiastical history of Illyricum from the apostles to the present day. It will run to eight folio volumes. Every diocese in it that once had a Catholic bishop is being looked up by the chancery to see who holds the town now, and increasingly the answer is that we do: Shkodër, Lezha and the hill country behind them, and the archbishop's seat at Skopje from which the missions to Serbia and Bulgaria have always been run.

The Illyrian name has been a claim made by scholars for two hundred years. It is now a jurisdiction.

There is money for one great work, and two proposals for it.

options.text: Build the shrine. Let Christendom come to us.

modifiers.name: The Pilgrim Road
modifiers.text: The Holy House is said to have rested on the cliff above the Rijeka crossing before it went on to Loreto, and pilgrims have believed it for four hundred years. Inns, candle makers, badge sellers and money changers line the road to the sanctuary, and the crown takes its share of every one of them.

options.text: Endow the colleges. Rome has the greater need.

modifiers.name: The Congregation's Men
modifiers.text: The best educated men in the kingdom are Rome's to dispose of, and they go: to Albania, to the Danube, to any court that needs somebody who can write in three alphabets and be trusted with a letter. The endowments that trained them leave with them and are never taxed again.

units.name: Banderium
units.text: The mailed retinue of a great house, raised under its own banner and its own arms. Splendidly mounted and heavy in the charge, slow to assemble, and travelling with a lord's baggage rather than a soldier's.

units.name: Haramije
units.text: Paid frontier foot, raised in 1539 to hunt Ottoman raiders through the woods and river country of the Sava and the Una. Fast, cheap and lightly armed, and never intended to hold a line of battle.

units.name: Slavonian Frontiersmen
units.text: The soldier households planted on the recovered Sava bank after 1699. Thirty souls under one roof work land the crown does not tax, and the men of it turn out armed when called. Good shots in their own woods, and not a storming column.

units.name: Croat Light Horse
units.text: Frontier cavalry hired into the German war, unequalled at scouting, pursuit and the ruin of a countryside. They will not stand in a firefight, and the linen scarf at their throats gave Europe the cravat.

buildings.name: Glagolitic Parish
buildings.text: A village church whose priest says Mass in Slavonic from a missal in Glagolitic letters, under a papal privilege granted to the bishop of Senj in 1248 and never withdrawn. He is married, he owns few books, and his congregation understands every word he says. Can only be built where the people actually speak the tongue the privilege covers.

buildings.name: Tricesima Station
buildings.text: A royal customs office with a weigh-house, a strong room and a guard, taking one part in thirty from every load that passes between the interior and the sea. The revenue is the crown's, not the town's, and the stations stand only where the traffic can be made to stop.

buildings.name: Glagolitic Press
buildings.text: A chapter press with cut Glagolitic type, of the kind Blaž Baromić brought back from Venice to Senj in 1493 and Šimun Kožičić Benja set up in his own house at Rijeka in 1530. Small, clerical, and printing books that no other press in Latin Christendom is permitted to print.

where.text: Paper is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Chapter Fortress
buildings.text: A cathedral precinct walled and towered at the chapter's own expense, on the model of the Zagreb Kaptol between 1512 and 1520. The canons hold the keys and pay the garrison, and when the raiders come the parish comes inside.

buildings.name: Illyrian College
buildings.text: A residential college on the model of Loreto and San Girolamo, taking boys from Slavic lands and turning out priests who can preach in the tongue their people speak. Its graduates go where bishops cannot, and its library is the best in the province.

buildings.name: Frontier Blockhouse
buildings.text: A timber watch-house with a firing platform and an alarm gun, one of a chain built within sight of each other along the cordon, and the soldier households settled around it who hold their land against hereditary service. It is only worth building on the border, and the border moves.

buildings.name: Generalcy Seat
buildings.text: The headquarters of a frontier generalcy, where the captaincies of the cordon are mustered, paid and inspected. There were two, at Karlovac and at Varaždin, and it can stand nowhere else.

buildings.name: Caravan Scala
buildings.text: The customhouse and bonded yard at the quay of Split, where the Bosnian caravans come down with wool, hides and wax and go back inland with cloth. The trade was turned here by argument and not by war.

buildings.name: Free Port
buildings.text: Under the free port patents the duty is remitted and the goods lie bonded in the crown's own sheds, waiting for a hull. Only Rijeka and Senj, where the roads from the interior reach the sea, hold such a patent.

buildings.name: Royal Academy
buildings.text: The Zagreb college of a dissolved order, taken over by the crown in 1776 with its library, lecture rooms and professors. Philosophy, theology and law are taught to the men who will staff the kingdom's offices.

buildings.name: Frontier Council
buildings.text: The war council of the frontier, sitting in this kingdom's capital instead of somebody else's. Muster rolls, magazines, engineers and the whole artillery establishment of the line are administered from one table, and the noble houses that supply its officers are heard at it.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Marian Shrine
buildings.text: A hill sanctuary with a miraculous image, a religious house to keep it, and a track worn smooth by people who walk it barefoot. They come from three kingdoms, they arrive believing, and a good many of them do not go home.

list.name: Loca Credibilia
list.text: The places of authentic faith. From the decree of 1231 a legal act had to be recorded before a cathedral chapter or a monastic convent, and Louis I fixed in 1351 the roll of houses whose seal made an instrument authentic. The chapter of Zagreb, sealing under the image of Saint Stephen since 1297, and the collegiate chapter of Čazma, founded in 1232 by bishop Stjepan II, drew, sealed and stored the charters of the realm, walked the boundaries of disputed land, served summonses and carried out judgments in the king's name. Western Europe hired lay notaries for this work. Here canons did it, and went on doing it until feudal tenure was abolished in the 1840s.

list.name: Sabor Kraljevine
list.text: The congregation of the realm, first recorded at Zagreb in 1273 and merged on 1 September 1558 into one assembly for Croatia and Slavonia. Prelates, magnates, the ban, the viceban, the protonotary and the deputies of the counties sat together: they voted the dika laid on each hearth, called out the noble insurrection, and the bishops brought banderia of their own. The diet had no fixed seat and answered a summons wherever the ban sent it, which is how it came to sit in the castle at Cetin on 1 January 1527 and elect Ferdinand of Habsburg king of Croatia on its own authority, after taking his oath to the kingdom's laws and liberties.

list.name: Visitationes Canonicae
list.text: From 1615 the archdeacons of Zagreb rode a circuit of every parish in the diocese and wrote each one down: the priest and what he could read, the church and its vessels, the parish fields and their yield, the confraternities, the number of houses and souls, and the conduct of the people in them. Two hundred and fourteen bound volumes of protocols survive from 1615 onward. It is the nearest thing this kingdom has to a census, kept by clergymen for a crown that cannot pay surveyors, and along the frontier it is also the register of which villages hold to the Greek rite and which have come over.

list.name: Tabula Banalis
list.text: Charles VI erected the Banal Table in 1723 and gave the kingdom a bench that sat all year, in place of the octaval terms under which a suit could outlive the man who brought it. The ban or his viceban presided over seven to nine judges with the protonotary of the realm as reporter; the court took the great causes at first instance and the appeals of the county courts, and from 1725 the king named its members. Its docket was land: who owned what in a country that had been overrun, emptied and granted out again, and no field in Slavonia was worth clearing until that question had an answer.
